profile.research_note:
Operator field corrected from blank to TierPoint based on the facility own name (source data left operator blank). Reused operator-level research from twoai_dc_operators row: TierPoint.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] TierPoint is headquartered at 12444 Powerscourt Drive, Suite 450, in St. Louis, Missouri, and traces to 2010, when the company acquired its first data center in Dallas, Texas. Argo Infrastructure Partners increased its ownership stake and capital commitment to TierPoint in a transaction reported in December 2025, following an earlier round in which TierPoint closed $320 million in equity from a consortium of investors.

The companys own site describes a portfolio of 40 data center facilities across 20 US markets coast-to-coast, serving thousands of companies spanning small businesses to Fortune 500 enterprises across both public and private sectors.

The registry here tracks 3 TierPoint facilities across three states, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, and Texas, a small subset of the companys 20 named markets. TierPoints origin in a 2010 Dallas acquisition and its continued Texas presence in this registry connect it to the same Dallas-Fort Worth corridor already carrying Stream, Digital Realty, and Aligned facilities recorded elsewhere in this registry. This specific facility, recorded in this registry as TierPoint Little Rock in Pulaski County, AR, was not individually named in the operator-level research above; its operator field was blank in the source data and is corrected here to TierPoint based on the facility own name, which unambiguously identifies its operator brand. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
TierPoint Little Rock publishes 9,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts, making it impossible to assess its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling.

The absence of a power figure is the binding constraint on understanding this facility's role in AI. Without megawatts, there is no path to calculating rack count, accelerator density, or actual compute capacity. The footprint is small by hyperscale standards. This facility cannot be ranked against AI infrastructure by the metric that determines scaling decisions.

The six certifications reveal what workloads this facility is built to host. SOC 1 Type 2 and ISO 27001 establish audited controls over financial systems and information security. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card processing. HIPAA and HITRUST together qualify it for protected health information, with HITRUST adding validated control frameworks beyond the regulatory baseline. ITAR qualifies it for defense-related technical data. None of these certifications addresses the high-density power infrastructure that AI training requires.

Arkansas has two facilities in this registry, neither publishing a megawatt figure. The state total is zero published MW. TierPoint Little Rock ranks first in the state only because no facility here publishes any power data. For readers evaluating whether this campus matters to AI, the data describes a compliance-oriented colocation facility of modest size with no published indicators of AI training or large-scale inference capacity.
